{{Short description|Example of a metacompact topological space that is not paracompact}}

In mathematics, the '''Dieudonné plank''' is a specific [[topological space]] introduced by {{harvs|txt|last=Dieudonné|year=1944|authorlink=Jean Dieudonné}}. It is an example of a [[metacompact space]] that is not [[paracompact space|paracompact]].

The notion has since been generalized (by Barr et al.) to that of an absolute CR-epic space.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Barr |first1=Michael |last2=Kennison |first2=John |last3=Rafael |first3=R. |date=2009 |title=Searching for More Absolute CR-epic Spaces |url=http://www.tac.mta.ca/tac/volumes/22/3/22-03.pdf |journal=[[Theory and Applications of Categories]] |volume=22 |issue=3 |pages=54–76}}</ref>
